    AI Overview
    "Apollo" most commonly refers to the Greek god, the NASA space program, or various modern companies and technologies. Here are the primary definitions:
     
    1. Mythology (Greek & Roman) 
    • Deity of Many Talents: Apollo is the Olympian god of prophecy, music, song, poetry, archery, healing, plague, and protection of the young.
    • Key Attributes: Often depicted with a golden bow and arrows, or a lyre. He is the patron deity of Delphi and is associated with light and the sun.
    • Symbols: Laurel wreath, raven, lyre, and bow. 
    2. NASA Apollo Program (1961–1972) 
    • Goal: The United States program that landed the first humans on the Moon.
    • Major Milestone: Apollo 11 successfully landed Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon on July 20, 1969.
    • Legacy: The program involved 12 men walking on the Moon and spanned 17 missions (including uncrewed tests), ending with Apollo 17 in 1972. 
    3. Modern Companies & Technology 
    • Apollo Global Management: A major global alternative investment manager.
    • Apollo GraphQL: A company that provides a popular platform for implementing GraphQL in software development.
    • Apollo Neuro: A wearable device aimed at stress management and improving sleep through touch therapy.
    • Apollo Scooters: A company specializing in electric scooters.
    • Apollo App: An AI application for accessing local and open-source language models. 
    4. Cultural 
    • The Apollo Theater: A famous music hall in Harlem, New York City, known for its influence on American culture and talent showcases.

    What exactly is Apollo the god of?
    The national divinity of the Greeks, Apollo has been recognized as a god of archery, music and dance, truth and prophecy, healing and diseases, the Sun and light, poetry, and more. He is the son of Zeus and Leto, and the twin brother of Artemis, goddess of the hunt.

    Which astronaut read from the Bible?
    During their ninth orbit of the Moon astronauts Bill Anders, Jim Lovell, and Frank Borman recited verses 1 through 10 of the Genesis creation narrative from the King James Bible. Anders read verses 1–4, Lovell verses 5–8, and Borman read verses 9 and 10.

    0:25
    Apollo 8 and Artemis II Here we see the path Apollo 8 took to the moon on the bottom pane, compared with the planned trajectory for Artemis II, set to launch this Wednesday, April 1st. Apollo 8 was the first crewed mission (to the moon) during the Apollo era of space flight. It orbited the moon 10 times and returned to Earth after a 6 day mission. Artemis II will not spend time orbiting the moon, but will use the lunar gravity to redirect its course and send it back to Earth after a quick flyby. Similarly, this will be the first crewed mission to then moon in the modern era of space exploration.     I'm genuinely excited to see America headed back to the Moon. But Artemis is a moondoggle and shows we haven't learned the deepest lessons of the Apollo era. Remember that Apollo did *not* result in durable progress in space. It marked a literal high point for more than half a century. The cost of space access remained prohibitively high until we had a rebirth of space entrepreneurship. Thank you for showing the way, SpaceX. Apollo was history's greatest tech demo—the Moon landing. This is inspiring—it shows the triumph of ingenuity, science, and reason. But also, Apollo led to half a century of stasis and regression. It was fundamentally uneconomic, contributed to creation of a cost-insensitive space agency and supply base, all more concerned with perpetuating their own existence, more concerned with make-work jobs than accelerating human progress.
